_comment: Golden-file regression baseline for pages 11-73 of the reference book. Established 2026-07-05, updated after resolving pages 24/33 misattribution, then again after adding GeneralWordFix/PhraseBigramDisambiguator (chechen_words.txt/chechen_phrases.txt now in active use). See tests/golden/test_manual_proofread_regression.py. Contains no book text -- safe to commit.
notes: overall_word_similarity_ratio measures whole-text agreement (difflib word-level SequenceMatcher.ratio) and includes non-palochka OCR noise (merged words, footnote markers, punctuation) that this pipeline was never designed to fix.

palochka_recall is the stricter, in-scope metric: fraction of expected words containing Ӏ that appear verbatim (whole word, not just the palochka) in the pipeline output. This is a lower bound -- a word can have the palochka correctly placed but still count as 'not recovered' if some other, out-of-scope OCR error remains elsewhere in the same word.

Pages 24 and 33 were originally excluded as 'missing_in_raw' -- their raw OCR blocks existed but were misattributed to pages 19 and 31 respectively. Resolved once the project owner supplied the original scan photos confirming both the visible printed page number and a near-verbatim text match; see tests/golden/manual_resolutions.py.
Remaining excluded pages (29, 30, 31) are photos that only captured part of the printed page (text starts mid-sentence) -- a scan-completeness problem, not a pipeline defect.

GeneralWordFix (non-palochka Cyrillic letter-confusion, e.g. ъ/ь, а/з, ha/kha, using chechen_words.txt) added ~0.0008 overall similarity with no palochka_recall regression -- small but genuine and verified safe. PhraseBigramDisambiguator (context-based tiebreak for ambiguous palochka candidates, using chechen_phrases.txt bigrams) fired zero times on this corpus: the phrase corpus is from an entirely different, unrelated book (appears to be a religious/Ezekiel-style translation), so bigram coverage for this novel's specific ambiguous words is essentially nil in practice. Neither harmful nor currently beneficial on this book; kept since it's still a sound mechanism that could help on a different book or with more corpus overlap.

WordSegmentationFix (splits merged/no-space OCR tokens using chechen_words.txt word-break decomposition) was found NET HARMFUL on real data and is excluded from the default pipeline (see build_pipeline()'s docstring and word_segmentation.py's module docstring for the full finding): Chechen's agglutinative morphology means many real words simply missing from the 75k-word dictionary coincidentally decompose into two other valid dictionary words, causing false-positive splits. This dropped overall similarity to ~83.8% (unhardened) / ~91.0% (after raising MIN_TOKEN_LENGTH/MIN_PIECE_LENGTH) -- both below the ~92.3% baseline without it. The corrector remains in the codebase, fully unit-tested, for explicit opt-in use with this tradeoff understood.
See tests/golden/manual_resolutions.py for the fully audited table of page-attribution fixes applied before these metrics were computed.
